notes: Supervisor: one worker thread per stream owns the state machine; each attempt is a private FfmpegDecoder (_decoder.py) with a frames reader (readinto into one reused bytearray, one bytes copy per frame), a stderr drain (ring of 24 lines) and, only when on_audio is set, an audio thread on a loopback TCP listener (audio_url tcp://127.0.0.1:<port>, loopback peers only, even-length chunks). Popen uses CREATE_NO_WINDOW, stdin DEVNULL, bufsize 0 and is assigned to the job right after spawn. The worker polls every 100 ms (woken early by first frame / EOF / stop / switch) for exit, stall (no frame or no first frame for stall_timeout) and switch. stop() kills the child, joins the worker (which reaps ffmpeg and joins drain threads), releases the lease and sets STOPPED; no on_frame after it returns.

Measured: ffmpeg's own TCP connect on Windows never reports a refused port and waits for its -timeout (5.5 s with -timeout 5000000; it hung >30 s without one), which broke test_max_retries (3 attempts > 15 s). Each attempt therefore first does a non-blocking Python TCP probe (_netprobe.py, abortable by stop, ~2 s on refusal) and skips the ffmpeg spawn when the camera is unreachable. build_ffmpeg_args adds '-timeout 5000000' for rtsp URLs as a backstop, plus -hide_banner -nostdin -loglevel error and the low-probe flags.

ffmpeg stderr echoes the full RTSP URL with the password ('Error opening input file rtsp://user:pass@...'). All stderr text is scrubbed (raw URL, raw and percent-decoded password) before it goes into reasons or logs.

hwaccel fallback: an attempt with hardware decoding that dies before its first frame and whose stderr mentions hwaccel/hardware/d3d11/dxva/the hwaccel name switches to software at once (not counted as a retry or reconnect). Network failures (refused, 404, 453) do not trigger it, so a camera that is down at startup keeps d3d11va. If ffmpeg reports 'Failed setup for format' (it silently decodes in software), stats()['decoder'] says 'software'.

If the camera has no audio track, ffmpeg 8.1 refuses '-map 0:a:0?' with 'Output file does not contain any stream' and exits. The supervisor detects this and continues video-only (not counted as a failure).

Backoff: doubles per failed attempt up to backoff_max, resets after a frame; while the last frame is < 30 s old the delay is capped at 0.5 s. max_retries counts consecutive attempts with no frame; FAILED releases the lease. stats()['reconnects'] counts retries after a failure or drop.
Pipe reads: ffmpeg writes rawvideo in 32 KiB blocks, so a 640x360 frame takes ~22 readinto calls and 1280x720 ~85. Acceptable at 15 fps; not tuned further.

RecordingDownloader writes to hidden temp files beside out_path (.<stem>.<token>.part.ts / .part.mp4), remuxes to the temp mp4 and os.replace()s it, so a failed download never touches an existing out_path. Cancel raises DownloadCancelled (new TapoError subclass in downloader.py, listed in __all__). Progress comes from X-Data-PTS relative to the first part over the clip duration (capped at 0.99, 33-bit wrap handled), then exactly 1.0 after the MP4 is in place. The remux ffmpeg is assigned to default_job(). Notifications disk_status/offline, stream_finish and connection_closed raise; heartbeat/unknown are ignored.

MediaSession: Digest over one keep-alive connection (reconnects if the 401 says Connection: close), maps 401-after-auth -> TapoAuthError, 503 or -52407 -> StreamLimitError, socket errors/timeouts -> TapoConnectionError with no secret in the message. parts() raises TapoConnectionError when no data arrives within the session timeout. It remembers session_id from the first JSON result and adds X-Session-Id to later send_json calls when absent.
find_ffmpeg: a TAPO_FFMPEG that points to a missing file is logged and the search continues (was an open contract question; not tested).
Known limit: cancel is checked between parts, so a cancel during a silent camera waits up to the session timeout (10 s default).
